mainTopic: The sources for the disasters of ט׳ באב, and how joy goes down in אב and up in אדר
overview: This amud opens with the last line of the earlier discussion about the עבודה זרה in the בית המקדש. The גמרא then goes through the משנה's list of disasters that happened on ט׳ באב. First it uses the dates in the פסוקים to show that the מרגלים returned, and the people cried, on the night of ט׳ באב. Along the way, אביי explains that תמוז had 30 days that year. ה׳ answered their crying for nothing by making that night a time of crying for all generations. Next, a ברייתא fits together two פסוקים about the first בית המקדש, which give the seventh and the tenth: the fire was set late on the ninth. רבי יוחנן would have chosen the tenth for the fast, but the רבנן mark the start of the disaster. The second בית המקדש, ביתר, and the plowing of the city follow, along with stories of a Roman officer who saved רבן גמליאל and of the young כהנים who gave the keys back to ה׳. The amud ends with רב's teaching that once אדר begins, we increase our joy.

steps.title: Closing line: You want to destroy the House
steps.stepSummary: The previous discussion ends with a saying tied to the עבודה זרה in the בית המקדש: you want to destroy the House, and I have given you a hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: You want to destroy the House; I have given you your hand.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the final line of the earlier discussion about the עבודה זרה placed in the בית המקדש. It is not the start of a new topic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The saying presents it as though one idol is speaking to another: you are trying to bring about the destruction of the בית המקדש, and I am helping you. The point is that the idol worship itself was pushing toward the חורבן.

keyTerms.meaning: The House, meaning the בית המקדש
I have handed over / given over

phrases.english: You want to destroy the House —
phrases.notes: The letter in square brackets is part of the corrected wording. "The House" is the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: I have given you your hand.
phrases.notes: Literally, "your hand I have handed over to it." In other words, I am helping you do it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the earlier discussion, which began before this section, about the idol in the בית המקדש.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The idol worship in the בית המקדש is described as actively helping bring about its destruction.

steps.title: Where do we know the decree on ט׳ באב came from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה, which says the decree against entering the Land was on תשעה באב, and asks for the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: On ט׳ באב it was decreed on our ancestors that they would not enter the Land. How do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה and asking how we know the date. This sets up the long calendar proof that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה tells the story of the מרגלים but never directly says it happened on תשעה באב. So the גמרא wants to show, from the dates in the פסוקים, that the decree really fell on that day.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?

phrases.english: On the Ninth of Av
it was decreed upon our ancestors
that they would not enter the Land.
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה, about the decree that followed the sin of the מרגלים.

phrases.english: From where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה, after the earlier discussion has ended.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source from the פסוקים showing that the decree against entering the Land happened on תשעה באב.

steps.title: Starting point: the משכן was set up in the second year
steps.stepSummary: The proof begins: the משכן was set up on 1 ניסן of the second year, and a teaching says that was the same year the מרגלים were sent.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: "In the first month of the second year, on the first of the month, the משכן was set up." And מר said: In the first year משה made the משכן; in the second year he set it up and sent the מרגלים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer by fixing a starting date: the משכן went up on the first of ניסן in the second year after leaving מצרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teaching of "the Master" ties two events to the same year: setting up the משכן and sending the מרגלים. Now the גמרא only has to count forward within that second year to reach the date of the decree.

keyTerms.meaning: And the Master said (introduces a known teaching)

phrases.english: As it is written:
"And it came to pass in the first month in the second year,
phrases.notes: שמות 40:17

phrases.english: on the first of the month, that the Tabernacle was erected."
And the Master said:

phrases.aramaic: שָׁנָה רִאשׁוֹנָה עָשָׂה מֹשֶׁה אֶת הַמִּשְׁכָּן,
phrases.english: In the first year, Moshe made the Tabernacle;
in the second, Moshe set up the Tabernacle
and sent the spies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The count starts from 1 ניסן of the second year, the year the מרגלים were sent.

steps.title: The cloud lifted on the twentieth of the second month
steps.stepSummary: The camp left סיני on 20 אייר, when the cloud rose from the משכן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is written: "In the second year, in the second month, on the twentieth of the month, the cloud lifted from the Tabernacle of the Testimony."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds the next date in the count: the people began traveling on 20 אייר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The cloud lifting was the signal to travel, so this פסוק shows the journey from סיני began on 20 אייר. Every later step counts forward from this day.

phrases.english: And it is written:
"And it came to pass in the second year, in the second month,
phrases.notes: במדבר 10:11. The second month is אייר.

phrases.english: on the twentieth of the month,
the cloud was taken up from the Tabernacle of the Testimony."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the next date to the calendar begun in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: The date the people left סיני

steps.title: Three days of travel, and turning away from God
steps.stepSummary: They traveled three days from the mountain of ה׳, and רבי חמא בר חנינא says that on that day they turned away from God.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is written: "They traveled from the mountain of ה׳ three days' journey." רבי חמא בר חנינא said: That day they turned away from following ה׳.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds three days of travel to the count. Along the way it quotes רבי חמא בר חנינא, who explains the people's attitude when they left.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the calendar, what matters is the three days: 20 אייר plus three days brings us to 23 אייר. רבי חמא בר חנינא's comment adds a spiritual point, that leaving סיני was already the start of turning away.

keyTerms.meaning: They turned away from following ה׳

phrases.english: And it is written:
"And they set forward from the mount of the Lord three days' journey."
phrases.notes: במדבר 10:33

phrases.english: Rabbi Chama bar Chanina said:
That very day they turned away from following the Lord.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְתִיב: ״וַיִּסְעוּ מֵהַר ה׳ דֶּרֶךְ שְׁלֹשֶׁת יָמִים״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds three days of travel to 20 אייר.
steps.raayaObject: Three more days in the count

steps.title: A month of eating meat brings us to the twenty-second of סיון
steps.stepSummary: The people craved meat and ate it for a whole month, which brings the count to 22 סיון.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is written: "The mixed crowd among them had a craving, and the Children of Israel also wept again." And it is written: "For a whole month." That brings us to 22 סיון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds the month the people spent eating meat after they complained. The total now reaches 22 סיון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Counting a month from 23 אייר, and since אייר has only 29 days, the month ends on 22 סיון. The story of the craving explains why they stayed in one place for that month.

keyTerms.meaning: The mixed crowd (non-Jews who left מצרים with the people)

phrases.english: And it is written:
"And the mixed multitude that was among them fell a lusting,
phrases.notes: במדבר 11:4

phrases.aramaic: וַיָּשֻׁבוּ וַיִּבְכּוּ גַּם בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְגוֹ׳״,
phrases.english: and the Children of Israel also wept again, etc."
And it is written:
"For a whole month, etc." —
phrases.notes: במדבר 11:20

phrases.english: which comes to the twenty-second of Sivan.
phrases.notes: 20 אייר plus three days of travel is 23 אייר. A month later lands on 22 סיון.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a month to the count from step 5.
steps.raayaObject: A month added to the count, reaching 22 סיון

steps.title: מרים's seven days bring us to the twenty-ninth of סיון, and the מרגלים are sent
steps.stepSummary: The people waited seven days for מרים, reaching 29 סיון, and then the פסוק says the מרגלים were sent.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is written: "מרים was shut out for seven days." That brings us to 29 סיון. And it is written: "Send men for yourself."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds the seven days the camp waited for מרים, which brings the count to 29 סיון. Right after that comes the command to send the מרגלים. The next step continues the count from this date.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 22 סיון plus seven days equals 29 סיון. Since the very next story in the תורה is sending the מרגלים, the גמרא has now fixed the day they left, and from there it can count forward toward תשעה באב.

keyTerms.meaning: She was shut out (kept outside the camp)
Send men for yourself (the opening of the spies story)

steps.whatToRemember: Step by step from the פסוקים: 20 אייר, then 3 days of travel, then a month of meat (22 סיון), then 7 days for מרים (29 סיון), and then the מרגלים are sent.
steps.whyThisMatters: Fixing the day the מרגלים left is the key piece the גמרא needs to show their return and the decree fell on תשעה באב.

phrases.english: And it is written:
"And Miriam was shut out for seven days" —
phrases.notes: במדבר 12:15

phrases.english: which comes to the twenty-ninth of Sivan,
and it is written: "Send you men,"
phrases.notes: במדבר 13:2

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds seven days to 22 סיון and reaches the sending of the מרגלים.
steps.raayaObject: The date the מרגלים were sent: 29 סיון

steps.title: The מרגלים were sent on 29 סיון and returned after forty days
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא confirms that משה sent the מרגלים on 29 סיון. The פסוק says they came back after forty days, which brings the count to ט׳ באב.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is taught in a ברייתא: on the twenty-ninth of סיון, משה sent the מרגלים. And the פסוק says: "They returned from scouting the land at the end of forty days."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up its count. The מרגלים left on 29 סיון, and adding forty days should bring us to ט׳ באב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 reached 29 סיון by counting. Now a ברייתא states that date directly. The פסוק of forty days is the last piece needed to land the spies' return on ט׳ באב.

keyTerms.meaning: It is taught in a ברייתא
Spies, the scouts משה sent into ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: And it is taught in a ברייתא:
On the twenty-ninth of Sivan
Moshe sent spies,
And it is written: "And they returned from scouting the land
at the end of forty days."
phrases.notes: במדבר 13:25

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנְיָא: בְּעֶשְׂרִים וְתִשְׁעָה בְּסִיוָן שָׁלַח מֹשֶׁה מְרַגְּלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms with a ברייתא the date reached by counting in step 7, and adds the forty days of scouting.
steps.raayaObject: That the spies returned, and the people cried, on ט׳ באב
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא dating the sending to 29 סיון, and במדבר 13:25 on the forty days

steps.title: The count comes out one day short
steps.stepSummary: Counting forty days from 29 סיון gives only 39 days until ט׳ באב.
steps.simpleTranslation: But these forty days are really forty minus one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks the math and finds a problem. From 29 סיון to ט׳ באב there are only 39 days, not forty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depends on the forty days landing exactly on ט׳ באב. If the count gives 39 days, the return would fall on the eighth of אב, and the proof breaks.

phrases.english: These forty days
are one short!
phrases.notes: Count it: the last days of סיון, a 29-day תמוז, and 8 days of אב come to only 39.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי אַרְבָּעִים יוֹם נְכֵי חַד הָווּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the arithmetic of the proof in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that forty days from 29 סיון reaches ט׳ באב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The calendar math gives 39 days, so the forty days do not end on ט׳ באב.

steps.title: אביי: That year תמוז had thirty days
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that תמוז was a full 30-day month that year, which supplies the missing day. He hints to this from a פסוק in איכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: That year they made תמוז a full month, as it says: "He called an appointed time against me to crush my young men."
steps.whatsHappening: אביי solves the counting problem. That year תמוז had 30 days instead of 29, so the forty days do end on ט׳ באב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Months in the Jewish calendar have either 29 or 30 days. The challenge assumed a 29-day תמוז. אביי says it had 30 days that year, which fixes the count, and he reads the פסוק as hinting to an added day so the disaster would land on ט׳ באב.

keyTerms.meaning: They made it full, a 30-day month

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not adding a day to the forty days. The forty days stay the same; he is saying the month of תמוז was longer that year, so the date lands one day later.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Tammuz of that year
they made it full,
phrases.notes: A full month has 30 days, and that gives us the missing day.

phrases.english: as it is written: "He called an appointed time against me
to crush my young men."
phrases.notes: איכה 1:15

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: תַּמּוּז דְּהַהִיא שַׁתָּא מַלּוֹיֵי מַלְּיוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the counting problem raised in step 9.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: תמוז had its usual 29 days, so the count reaches only the eighth of אב.
steps.terutzMaskana: That year תמוז had 30 days, so the forty days end exactly on ט׳ באב.

steps.title: The night of crying was ט׳ באב
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says the people cried that night. רבה in the name of רבי יוחנן says it was the night of ט׳ באב, and ה׳ set it as a time of crying for all generations.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: "The whole congregation raised their voice, and the people cried that night." רבה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: That night was the night of ט׳ באב‎. ה׳ said to them: You cried for no reason, so I will set a crying for you for generations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof. When the מרגלים returned, the people cried, and that night was ט׳ באב, so the decree against the generation in the desert came on ט׳ באב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the count now fixed, the night after the spies' report falls on ט׳ באב. רבי יוחנן adds the meaning: since they cried over nothing, ה׳ made that date a day of real crying for the future. This explains why later tragedies fell on the same date.

keyTerms.meaning: Crying for nothing, without a real reason

steps.whatToRemember: The sin of the מרגלים and the people's crying happened on the night of ט׳ באב. Because that crying was for nothing, ה׳ made ט׳ באב a day of crying for all generations.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the root of ט׳ באב as a day of mourning. The later tragedies listed in the משנה fall on the date first set by the מרגלים.

phrases.english: And it is written: "And the whole congregation raised up
and gave forth their voice
and the people cried that night,"
phrases.notes: במדבר 14:1

phrases.english: Rabba said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:

phrases.aramaic: אוֹתוֹ לַיְלָה לֵיל תִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב הָיָה.
phrases.english: That night was the night of the Ninth of Av.
The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to them:
You cried a crying for nothing,
and I will set for you a crying for generations.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְתִיב: ״וַתִּשָּׂא כׇּל הָעֵדָה וַיִּתְּנוּ אֶת קוֹלָם וַיִּבְכּוּ הָעָם בַּלַּיְלָה הַהוּא״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: With the count fixed in step 10, this step names the night of crying as ט׳ באב and closes the proof.
steps.raayaObject: That the decree against the generation in the desert was on ט׳ באב
steps.raayaSupportSource: במדבר 14:1, explained by רבה in the name of רבי יוחנן
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The people's crying after the spies' report was on ט׳ באב, and that day became a day of crying for the generations.

steps.title: The first בית המקדש was destroyed: the פסוק in מלכים says the seventh
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the משנה's next item, the destruction of the first בית המקדש. It quotes a פסוק in מלכים that dates the burning to the seventh of the fifth month.
steps.simpleTranslation: The בית המקדש was destroyed the first time, as it says: "In the fifth month, on the seventh of the month, in the nineteenth year of King נבוכדנאצר of Babylon, נבוזראדן the chief of the guards, servant of the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem and burned the House of ה׳."
steps.whatsHappening: A new section starts. The גמרא now looks for the source that the first בית המקדש was destroyed on ט׳ באב, and begins with a פסוק that gives the date as the seventh of אב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fifth month counted from ניסן is אב. But this פסוק says the seventh, not the ninth, so it does not yet prove the משנה's claim on its own. It sets up the comparison with the next פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: The fifth month, אב, counting from ניסן

phrases.english: The Temple was destroyed the first time,
as it is written: "And in the fifth month,
on the seventh of the month,
which was the nineteenth year
of King Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon,
Nebuzaradan, chief of the guards, came,
a servant of the king of Babylon, to Jerusalem.
And he burned the House of ה׳, etc."
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 25:8–9

steps.triggerLanguage: חָרַב הַבַּיִת בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה, דִּכְתִיב: ״וּבַחֹדֶשׁ הַחֲמִישִׁי בְּשִׁבְעָה לַחֹדֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the מרגלים and opens the next item of the משנה, the first destruction.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first בית המקדש was destroyed in the fifth month (אב); the source begins with מלכים ב 25:8–9.

steps.title: The פסוק in ירמיהו says the tenth
steps.stepSummary: A second פסוק, in ירמיהו, describes the same event but dates it to the tenth of the fifth month. This clashes with the seventh and also does not say the ninth.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is written: "In the fifth month, on the tenth of the month, in the nineteenth year of King נבוכדנאצר of Babylon, נבוזראדן the chief of the guards, who stood before the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets two פסוקים side by side: one says the seventh, the other says the tenth. This sets up the next move, where the גמרא will need to explain how both fit, and how ט׳ באב fits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both פסוקים describe the same burning in the same year, yet give different days. Neither day is the ninth, so the גמרא must still explain the dates before the משנה's claim about ט׳ באב is proven.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא has proven ט׳ באב yet. So far it has only shown two פסוקים that disagree, the seventh and the tenth; the answer comes next.

phrases.english: And it is written: "And in the fifth month,
on the tenth of the month,
which was the nineteenth year
of King Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon,
Nebuzaradan, chief of the guards, came,

phrases.aramaic: עָמַד לִפְנֵי מֶלֶךְ בָּבֶל בִּירוּשָׁלִָם וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: who stood before the king of Babylon, into Jerusalem, etc."
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 52:12–13

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets a second פסוק against the one in step 12, creating a conflict of dates.
steps.kashyaTarget: The date of the destruction given in מלכים ב 25:8, and the משנה's claim of ט׳ באב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two פסוקים about the same event give the seventh and the tenth. They contradict each other, and neither matches the ninth.

steps.title: A ברייתא explains how both the seventh and the tenth are correct
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא resolves the clash between the two פסוקים. The enemy entered on the seventh, ate and damaged the היכל on the seventh and eighth, set it on fire late on the ninth, and the fire kept burning all the next day.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: You cannot say it happened on the seventh, because the פסוק says the tenth. You cannot say the tenth, because the other פסוק says the seventh. So how does it work? On the seventh the non-Jews entered the היכל. On the seventh and eighth they ate there and ruined it. On the ninth, close to dark, they set it on fire, and it kept burning the whole next day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the clash from Step 13 by bringing a ברייתא. The ברייתא shows that each date describes a different stage of the same event.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The seventh is when the enemy first came in, so 'בא' in מלכים means 'entered.' The fire started at the end of the ninth and kept going through the tenth, which is the date ירמיהו gives. This also answers why our משנה says the ninth: that is the day the burning began.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching of the תנאים that was not included in the משנה
How can this be? A phrase used to start reconciling two sources that seem to clash
The main sanctuary building of the בית המקדש

steps.confusionAlert: Nobody here is saying a פסוק is wrong. The seventh, ninth, and tenth are three stages of one disaster: entering, starting the fire, and the main burning.

phrases.english: And it is taught: It is impossible to say on the seventh,
since it already says "on the tenth."
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק in ירמיהו from Step 13.

phrases.english: And it is impossible to say on the tenth,
since it already says "on the seventh."
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק in מלכים from Step 12.

phrases.english: So how does it work?
On the seventh, non-Jews entered the היכל,
and they ate and ruined it on the seventh and the eighth.
And on the ninth, close to nightfall,
they set it on fire,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָיָה דּוֹלֵק וְהוֹלֵךְ כׇּל הַיּוֹם כּוּלּוֹ,
phrases.english: and it kept burning the entire day.
phrases.notes: He means the whole next day, the tenth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the clash raised in Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting one event into stages, each matching a different date
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two פסוקים give competing dates for one single act of burning, and neither one says the ninth.
steps.terutzMaskana: The seventh is the entry, the ninth is when the fire started, and the tenth is when the fire was burning. All the sources fit, and the ninth is the start of the burning.

steps.title: A פסוק shows the fire began toward evening
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא brings a פסוק about the day turning and evening shadows stretching out. This supports the claim that the fire was set close to dark.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: "Woe to us, for the day has turned, for the evening shadows stretch out."
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא supports its timeline with a פסוק. The פסוק shows the fire started as evening came.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'the day has turned' and 'evening shadows' are read as describing the moment of disaster. That fits the claim that the fire was lit late on the ninth, right before the tenth began.

keyTerms.meaning: The day has turned, meaning the day is ending

phrases.english: As it says: "Woe to us, for the day has turned,
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 6:4

phrases.english: for the evening shadows stretch out."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a פסוק to back up the time of day stated in Step 14.
steps.raayaObject: That the fire was set close to nightfall on the ninth
steps.raayaSupportSource: ירמיהו 6:4, which speaks of the day turning and evening shadows

steps.title: רבי יוחנן would have set the fast on the tenth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא links this timeline to רבי יוחנן's statement. He said that had he lived then, he would have fixed the fast on the tenth, because most of the היכל burned on that day.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what רבי יוחנן meant when he said: If I had lived in that generation, I would have set the fast only on the tenth, because most of the היכל burned on that day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רבי יוחנן's famous statement is based on this exact timeline.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the fire started only at the very end of the ninth, most of the destruction happened on the tenth. רבי יוחנן thinks the fast should match the day of the main damage.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what he meant. It ties an earlier statement to what we just learned
If only, or had it been that
I would have set it, meaning fixed the fast day

phrases.english: And this is what רבי יוחנן said:
Had I been in that generation,
I would have set it only on the tenth,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the fast of ט׳ באב.

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁרוּבּוֹ שֶׁל הֵיכָל בּוֹ נִשְׂרַף.
phrases.english: because most of the היכל burned on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Connects the ברייתא's timeline to רבי יוחנן's opinion about when the fast should be.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In רבי יוחנן's view, the fast should go on the day most of the destruction happened, which was the tenth.

steps.title: Why the רבנן chose the ninth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the רבנן, who fixed the fast on the ninth. They hold that the beginning of a disaster is the better day to mark.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן? The beginning of the disaster is more important.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an unspoken question: if most of the burning was on the tenth, why did the רבנן choose the ninth?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two sides disagree about which moment defines the tragedy. רבי יוחנן looks at the main damage. The רבנן look at the start of the disaster, which was the ninth, when the fire was set.
steps.whatToRemember: The fire began late on ט׳ באב and burned mostly on the tenth. We fast on the ninth because the רבנן mark the start of the disaster.

phrases.english: And the רבנן? The beginning of the disaster is preferable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends the accepted date against רבי יוחנן's argument.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different measure for choosing the date
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The fast should be on the tenth, the day of most of the destruction.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ninth is chosen because it is the start of the disaster.

steps.title: How do we know the second בית המקדש fell on ט׳ באב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the next item in the משנה and asks for the source that the second בית המקדש was also destroyed on ט׳ באב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the second time, how do we know?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source for the משנה's statement that the second בית המקדש was also destroyed on ט׳ באב. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the first בית המקדש, the גמרא worked out the date from פסוקים. For the second there are no such פסוקים, so a different kind of source is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: The second time, meaning the second בית המקדש

phrases.english: And the second time, from where do we know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the first בית המקדש to the second one in the משנה's list.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing the second בית המקדש was destroyed on ט׳ באב

steps.title: Bad events are drawn to a bad day
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that good things are brought about on a good day and bad things on a bad day. So the second destruction also came on ט׳ באב.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: Merit is rolled onto a good day, and guilt onto a bad day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. Since ט׳ באב was already a day of disaster, more disasters were brought on that day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source is not a פסוק about the date. It is a general rule that days carry a character. ט׳ באב already had disasters, so it was 'ready' for another one.

keyTerms.meaning: They roll, meaning events are brought about
A guilty day, a day already marked by disaster

phrases.english: As it is taught: Merit is rolled onto a meritorious day,
and guilt onto a guilty day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Bad events are brought about on a day that already has a bad history, so the second destruction also fell on ט׳ באב.

steps.title: The details of the day the first בית המקדש fell
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists the features of the day the first בית המקדש was destroyed. It was ט׳ באב, right after שבת, the year after שמיטה, during the week of the משמר of יהויריב, and the לויים were singing on their platform.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: When the first בית המקדש was destroyed, that day was ט׳ באב. It was right after שבת. It was the year after שמיטה. It was the week of the משמר of יהויריב. And the לויים were singing, standing on their platform.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a list of the matching features of the day the first בית המקדש fell. This sets up the story of the song in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list shows several details lining up on the same day. This fits the idea that disasters were drawn to a day already marked for them.

keyTerms.meaning: The end of שבת, meaning right after it
The year after the שמיטה year
A family group of כהנים that served in the בית המקדש during its assigned week
The platform where the לויים stood to sing

phrases.english: They said: When the בית המקדש was destroyed the first time,
that day was the ninth of Av,
and it was right after שבת,
and it was the year after the seventh year,
and it was the watch of יהויריב.
And the לויים were singing a song,
and standing on their platform.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא and fills in the details of the day of destruction.
steps.raayaObject: That the day of destruction was a day of several matching 'marked' features
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's description of the first destruction

steps.title: The לויים were cut off in the middle of their song
steps.stepSummary: The לויים were singing a פסוק about ה׳ bringing the wicked's sin back on them. Before they could finish 'ה׳ our God will cut them off,' the enemy came and conquered them.
steps.simpleTranslation: What song were they singing? "He turned their sin back on them, and He will cut them off through their evil." They did not manage to say "ה׳ our God will cut them off" before the non-Jews came and conquered them.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tells which song the לויים were singing, and that the enemy broke in before they could finish it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The song was about ה׳ punishing the wicked. The fact that it was cut off mid-פסוק shows how suddenly the destruction came.

keyTerms.meaning: He will cut them off, or destroy them
They did not manage, or did not have time

phrases.english: And what song were they singing?
"And He turned their sin back upon them,
phrases.notes: תהלים 94:23

phrases.english: and through their evil He will cut them off,"
and they did not manage to say
"ה׳ our God will cut them off,"
phrases.notes: This is the end of that same פסוק.

phrases.english: before non-Jews came and conquered them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story from Step 20 with the details of the song.
steps.raayaObject: How suddenly the destruction came on that day
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים 94:23, cut off in the middle

steps.title: The same happened with the second בית המקדש
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends by saying that the same thing happened when the second בית המקדש was destroyed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the same was true for the second one.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא closes by applying everything it said about the first destruction to the second one as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line directly answers the question of Step 18. The second בית המקדש also fell on ט׳ באב, under the same circumstances, which fits the rule that bad events are drawn to a bad day.
steps.whatToRemember: Both בתי המקדש fell on ט׳ באב. The first is shown from the פסוקים, and the second from the rule that disasters are drawn to an already bad day, along with the ברייתא's 'וכן בשניה.'

phrases.english: And likewise with the second.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the description of the first destruction to the second.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The second בית המקדש was also destroyed on ט׳ באב, in the same way as the first.

steps.title: ביתר's capture is known by tradition
steps.stepSummary: For the next item in the משנה, that ביתר was captured on ט׳ באב, the גמרא gives a one-word answer: it is a tradition.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said ביתר was captured on ט׳ באב. How do we know? It is a tradition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next item in the משנה, the fall of ביתר, and simply says we know it from a received tradition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the earlier items the גמרא brought פסוקים or ברייתות. Here there is no written source. The date is known only because it was handed down.

keyTerms.meaning: ביתר, the last stronghold of the בר כוכבא revolt
here: a received tradition, something learned and handed down

steps.confusionAlert: The word גמרא here does not mean 'the Talmud.' It means 'a tradition': we know this fact because it was handed down, not from a פסוק.

phrases.english: Beitar was captured:
It is a tradition.
phrases.notes: Here גמרא means 'something we have by tradition.' There is no פסוק for this one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the second בית המקדש to the next item in the משנה's ט׳ באב list
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Implied: what is the source that ביתר fell on ט׳ באב?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is known by received tradition

steps.title: The plowing of the היכל and the decree against רבן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: For 'the city was plowed,' the גמרא brings a ברייתא. When טורנוסרופוס plowed the היכל, a decree went out to execute רבן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the plowing of the city, a ברייתא teaches: when the wicked טורנוסרופוס plowed the היכל, a decree was issued that רבן גמליאל be killed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reaches the last item in the משנה, the plowing of the city. It brings a ברייתא that names who did the plowing and opens a story about רבן גמליאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא tells us who plowed: טורנוסרופוס, the Roman governor. It also sets up the danger to רבן גמליאל, which the next steps tell as a story.

keyTerms.meaning: טורנוסרופוס, the Roman governor of Judea
the Sanctuary building of the בית המקדש

phrases.english: The city was plowed:
It is taught in a ברייתא:
When the wicked Turnus Rufus plowed the Sanctuary,

phrases.aramaic: נִגְזְרָה גְּזֵרָה עַל רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל לַהֲרִיגָה.
phrases.english: a decree was issued against Rabban Gamliel to be killed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues to the last item in the משנה's list
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The plowing was done by טורנוסרופוס, and with it came a decree to kill רבן גמליאל

steps.title: The officer's hidden warning and רבן גמליאל's hiding
steps.stepSummary: A Roman officer came into the בית המדרש and called out, as a hint, that 'the man with the nose' was wanted. רבן גמליאל understood and went into hiding.
steps.simpleTranslation: That officer came, stood in the בית המדרש, and said: 'The man with the nose is wanted, the man with the nose is wanted.' רבן גמליאל heard this and hid from them.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. An officer gives רבן גמליאל a coded warning, and רבן גמליאל goes into hiding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The officer could not openly warn a Jewish leader, so he used a hint. 'The man with the nose' points to the most prominent person, the leader of the generation, and רבן גמליאל understood it was about him.

keyTerms.meaning: an officer or official of the Roman government
'the man with the nose,' a hint for the most prominent person

phrases.english: A certain officer came
and stood in the study hall, and said:
The man with the nose is wanted,
phrases.notes: This is a hidden hint. The leader stands out in his generation the way a nose stands out on a face.

phrases.english: the man with the nose is wanted.

phrases.aramaic: שָׁמַע רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל, אֲזַל טְשָׁא מִינַּיְיהוּ.
phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel heard, and went and hid from them.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּא אוֹתוֹ הֶגְמוֹן וְעָמַד בְּבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story begun by the ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The officer secretly warned רבן גמליאל, who hid

steps.title: The officer's deal: saving רבן גמליאל for a share in עולם הבא
steps.stepSummary: The officer went to רבן גמליאל in secret and asked: if I save you, will you bring me to עולם הבא? רבן גמליאל said yes and swore to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The officer went to him privately and said: 'If I save you, will you bring me into עולם הבא?' He answered: 'Yes.' The officer said: 'Swear to me.' And he swore to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The officer offers to save רבן גמליאל in exchange for a promise of עולם הבא, and he asks for an oath. This sets up the officer's act in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The officer does not ask for money or honor, only for a place in עולם הבא. Asking for an oath shows how much the promise meant to him, since he was about to give his life for it.

keyTerms.meaning: swear (as a command), or he swore

phrases.english: He went to him in private
and said to him: If I save you,
will you bring me into the World to Come?
He said to him: Yes.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לֵיהּ: אִשְׁתְּבַע לִי. אִשְׁתְּבַע לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: He said to him: Swear to me. He swore to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story: the officer makes his deal
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן גמליאל swore that the officer would have a share in עולם הבא

steps.title: The officer gives his life and the decree is cancelled
steps.stepSummary: The officer went up to the roof, fell, and died. The Romans had a rule that if one of them died after a decree, they cancelled the decree.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went up to the roof, fell, and died. They had a tradition that when they made a decree and one of them died, they would cancel the decree.
steps.whatsHappening: The officer sacrifices himself, and the גמרא explains why his death saved רבן גמליאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Romans took a death among themselves as a bad sign for the decree. By dying, the officer caused the decree against רבן גמליאל to be cancelled.

keyTerms.meaning: they had a tradition, it was known

phrases.english: He went up to the roof, fell, and died.
And they had a tradition that when they issue a decree
and one of them dies,
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the Romans who made the decree, not the Jews.

phrases.english: they cancel their decree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The officer carries out his side of the deal
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The officer's death cancelled the decree against רבן גמליאל

steps.title: A בת קול: the officer has earned עולם הבא
steps.stepSummary: A בת קול announced that the officer was ready for עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: A בת קול came out and said: 'That officer is designated for the life of עולם הבא.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with Heaven confirming that the officer's sacrifice earned him עולם הבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The officer asked רבן גמליאל for a promise, and here Heaven itself confirms it. A non-Jew who gave his life to save a leader of Israel was rewarded with עולם הבא.

keyTerms.meaning: the life of the World to Come

steps.whatToRemember: Even in the middle of the destruction, a Roman officer gave his life to save רבן גמליאל, and a בת קול declared that he earned עולם הבא.

phrases.english: A Heavenly voice came out and said:

phrases.aramaic: אוֹתוֹ הֶגְמוֹן מְזוּמָּן לְחַיֵּי הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא.
phrases.english: That officer is designated for the life of the World to Come.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the story with Heaven's answer
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The officer's self-sacrifice earned him עולם הבא

steps.title: Young כהנים bring the היכל keys to the roof
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that when the first בית המקדש was destroyed, groups of young כהנים went up to the roof of the היכל with its keys. They told ה׳ that since they had not been trustworthy keepers, the keys should be given back to Him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: when the בית המקדש was destroyed the first time, many groups of young כהנים gathered with the keys of the היכל in their hands. They went up to the roof of the היכל and said before ה׳: 'Master of the World, since we did not merit to be trustworthy treasurers, let the keys be handed over to You.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא about the destruction. This step sets up the scene, and the next step tells what happened to the keys.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The young כהנים felt they had failed at guarding the בית המקדש. So they gave the keys back to ה׳ instead of letting the enemy take them.

keyTerms.meaning: young כהנים, literally 'blossoms of the priesthood'
treasurers, those in charge of guarding

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
When the Temple was destroyed the first time,
group after group gathered together
of young priests,
with the keys of the Sanctuary in their hands,
and they went up to the roof of the Sanctuary
and said before Him: Master of the World!
Since we did not merit
to be trustworthy treasurers,
let the keys be handed over to You.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new ברייתא about the destruction of the first בית המקדש
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The young כהנים returned the keys of the היכל to ה׳

steps.title: A hand takes the keys and the priests jump into the fire
steps.stepSummary: The כהנים threw the keys upward, something like a hand came out and took them, and the כהנים jumped into the fire of the burning היכל.
steps.simpleTranslation: They threw the keys upward. Something like the palm of a hand came out and took them from them. And they jumped and fell into the fire.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends: Heaven accepts the keys, and the young כהנים die together with the בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The hand shows that ה׳ accepted the keys, so the בית המקדש was given back to Him and not simply taken by the enemy. The כהנים chose not to live on after the היכל they had served.
steps.whatToRemember: At the first destruction, the young כהנים gave the keys back to ה׳, a hand from Heaven took them, and the כהנים jumped into the fire.

phrases.english: And they threw them upward.
And something like the palm of a hand came out
and took them from them.
And they jumped and fell into the fire.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story of the keys
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Heaven took back the keys, and the young כהנים died together with the burning היכל

steps.title: ישעיהו laments over the young כהנים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings ישעיהו's lament (ישעיהו 22:1–2), which describes people who went up to the roofs and died, but not by the sword or in battle. The lament is read as speaking about the young כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: ישעיהו הנביא mourned over these כהנים: 'The burden of the Valley of Vision. What is wrong with you, that you have all gone up to the roofs? You were a noisy, busy, happy city. Your dead were not killed by the sword or in war.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא connects the story of the young כהנים to a פסוק in ישעיהו that mourns them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק has two details that match the story. 'Gone up to the roofs' fits the כהנים climbing onto the roof of the היכל. 'Not killed by the sword or in battle' fits their death, since they jumped into the fire and were not killed by enemies.

keyTerms.meaning: Lamented, mourned with words of grief
The Valley of Vision, a name the פסוק uses for the place being mourned

phrases.english: And over them the prophet Isaiah lamented:
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the young כהנים from the story just before this.

phrases.english: "The burden of the Valley of Vision.
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 22:1–2

phrases.english: What ails you now
that you have all gone up to the roofs?
Full of uproar, a tumultuous city,
a joyous town,
your slain are not slain by the sword
nor dead in battle."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ties the story of the כהנים in steps 29–30 to a פסוק of lament
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ישעיהו's lament about going up to the roofs and dying, but not in war, speaks about the young כהנים.

steps.title: Even הקדוש ברוך הוא cries out over the destruction
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds another פסוק (ישעיהו 22:5), which describes even הקדוש ברוך הוא as shouting and crying over the destruction.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even about הקדוש ברוך הוא the פסוק says: 'Shouting over the walls, and a cry to the mountain.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the story of the חורבן by showing that הקדוש ברוך הוא Himself joins in the mourning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'even' (אַף) is the key. It is not only the נביא who grieves. The same chapter describes הקדוש ברוך הוא as crying out over the walls and the mountain, so the sadness reaches all the way up.

keyTerms.meaning: A cry, a scream for help

steps.whatToRemember: The חורבן story ends with grief from every side. The כהנים gave back the keys, ישעיהו mourned them, and even הקדוש ברוך הוא is described as crying out.

phrases.english: Even regarding the Holy One, Blessed be He, it is said:
"Shouting over walls
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 22:5

phrases.english: and a cry to the mountain."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on ישעיהו's lament with a further פסוק from the same chapter
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The destruction is mourned even by הקדוש ברוך הוא, which closes the story of the חורבן.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: lowering joy once אב begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words that once אב begins, we lower our rejoicing. This opens a new discussion.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'From when אב begins, we decrease rejoicing,' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The story is over, and the גמרא now returns to the משנה. This line quotes the משנה to set up the next statement about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Quoting the משנה tells us which rule is about to be discussed. On its own it adds nothing new. It prepares for רב's teaching in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: We decrease, we do less of
Etc., and so on (the rest of the משנה)

phrases.english: From when Av begins
we decrease rejoicing, etc.
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting the משנה here. 'Etc.' means the rest of the line is assumed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story and returns to the text of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once אב begins, we lower our rejoicing.

steps.title: Just as joy goes down in אב, it goes up in אדר
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה בריה דרב שמואל בר שילת teaches in the name of רב that the opposite rule applies to אדר: once אדר begins, we increase our rejoicing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה, son of רב שמואל בר שילת, said in the name of רב: Just as we lower our joy when אב begins, we raise our joy when אדר begins.
steps.whatsHappening: רב takes the משנה's rule about אב and gives its mirror image for אדר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only speaks about sad times. רב adds a new rule using a 'just as... so too' pattern. אב, the month of sad events, makes us lower our joy, and אדר, the month of happy events, makes us raise it.

keyTerms.meaning: We increase, we do more of

steps.whatToRemember: There are two mirror rules. Once אב begins, we lower our joy (the משנה). Once אדר begins, we raise our joy (רב).
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaching is the source of the well-known saying 'משנכנס אדר מרבין בשמחה.'

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר שִׁילַת
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda, son of Rav Shmuel bar Sheilat, said
in the name of Rav:
Just as from when Av begins
we decrease rejoicing,
so too from when Adar begins
we increase rejoicing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר שִׁילַת מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a matching rule for אדר to the משנה's rule about אב
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once אדר begins, we increase our rejoicing, the mirror of lowering joy in אב.
